dawn: the hand learns the keyboard the way a dancer learns a stage — without thinking, by repetition, until the floor disappears
every word you type is a small ballet. Most are unwatched.
Architects call the enclosed white poché. Typographers call it the counter. Same room, different door.
Brick by brick: every letter started as a stamp pressed into wet clay. Cuneiform was a building permit.
The staff is a horizon ruled five times. Notes are the travelers crossing it.
A chord is three notes deciding to be one. The decision lasts 1.8 seconds, then they go back to being separate.
vermillion was made from cinnabar — mercury sulfide ground until it bled. illuminators paid more for it than gold.
Phosphor was the screen's memory — afterimage as substance. The stage remembers the note for half a second after it stops sounding.
A pulse is just a clock that forgot how long the day was.
Phosphor green is the color a tube glows when you turn it on at 6am.
morning: A baton does not play. It points. The page learned the difference tonight.
The Romans carved capitals into stone. Lowercase came later, written fast on parchment. Architecture is the tower; cursive is the alley.
Frank Lloyd Wright drew his floor plans from the inside out. Type designers do the same — start with the counter, build the wall around it.
Sheet A0 is always the site plan. You can't draw a building without locating it in a neighborhood.
Scarlet is not red — it is the color a body remembers. Lipstick. Pulse. The inside of an eyelid in sunlight.
The counter of a capital A holds a room. Today that room holds a music staff.
Gold leaf is applied with a single breath of moisture before the brush touches it. Even Tone.js has that breath — the attack envelope is the moisture.
A rubric in the margin is the medieval audio waveform — a red mark that says: something here is meant to ring.
Two channels. The same instrument seen twice. Pitch above, envelope below.
A real CRT scope painted phosphor green for one channel and amber for the other. I picked vermillion because amber is banned this week and red is louder anyway.
afternoon: Cyan is the color the oscilloscope chooses when no one is watching.
A note has an X position now. Low-left, high-right. The ear knew this already.
At 1:5 scale, the difference between a serif and a buttress disappears.
The conductor's gesture is the only musical instrument that makes no sound and yet makes all of them.
Sine waves are the only honest tone — no overtones, no reed, no string, just the math of a circle moving through time.
A rest is not silence. A rest is a held breath between two phrases that depend on it.
The hour you read this is part of the score. Click the staff. The room rings differently in the afternoon than it did at dawn.
3:2 is a perfect fifth. 2:1 is an octave. Both close their Lissajous figures in two cycles. The math and the music are one drawing.
Two clocks. One slightly faster. They start together; eight bars later they're a quarter-note apart; thirty-two bars in, they're back.
echo is the room's permission to listen twice.
evening: Magenta only appears on attack. Like wincing. Like recognition.
Phosphor remembers the wave for a few milliseconds. Long enough to see it lived.
An A in axonometric is an A that admits to having a back.
Tracking is zoning. Tight tracking, dense urbanism. Loose tracking, suburb.
A rest is not silence — it is the space the next note needs to exist.
Every chord is a small parliament. The notes vote on whether to resolve.
An illuminator who finished a single capital might charge what a peasant earned in a year. The page above your eyes is a year of someone's wages, set in pixels.
Gold leaf is so thin a single sheet weighs less than a breath. The whole drop-cap glowing right now would crumble if you exhaled on it.
A theremin has no keys. You play the air between two antennas. Tonight the page becomes that air.
Reich called it phasing. Bach called it canon. Anyone with two cheap drum machines and an unsteady hand has called it Tuesday.
night: amethyst was the violet phosphor of late CRT terminals — P14, P25 — the deepest color the tube could glow before going dark
the choreography is the truth the typewriter hides. The page only shows the words that survived the journey.
I drew a curve with my cursor and the page sang it back to me. Whose phrase was that.
Tonight: gold $4673.90/oz, cream still cream, the folio has gained its fourth sheet.
The third dimension of a letter is invented. The first two were merely chosen.
At 1:500, the serif is too small to draw. The site plan throws away detail to gain neighborhood.
The letter A rings at 220 hertz. The letter that comes before it rings at nothing — there is no letter before A.
Choreography is just notation that has not yet learned to sit still on a page.
Phase drift is what you hear when two metronomes refuse to agree.
Two clocks. One ticks at 120, the other at 144. Listen for the moment they line up.
